title: The Hidden Journey of a Pollen Grain
section: 讲话 / 报道 / 讲座
transcript:
A pollen grain found on a flower does not necessarily come from the nearest plant. Understanding its journey matters when conservationists decide how far apart patches of habitat can be placed. Simply counting the insects that visit each patch tells us something about local activity, but it does not reveal whether those visitors carry pollen between patches.

A research team investigated this question using a harmless fluorescent powder as a temporary marker. They applied a tiny quantity to selected flowers early in the morning, before insects became active. Later, they inspected flowers at different distances using a special lamp. The powder was easier to detect than natural pollen, although it could not tell them whether a visit had resulted in successful reproduction.

The most surprising result concerned a narrow strip of rough grass beside a drainage channel. Few insects remained there long enough to appear in the researchers' standard counts. Nevertheless, marked powder appeared on flowers beyond the strip more often when the grass had been left uncut. Video observations suggested that some insects used the strip as a sheltered route during windy conditions.

This finding changed the team's interpretation of an apparently unimportant piece of land. A location can support movement without attracting a large number of permanent residents. Removing it might therefore separate two productive habitats even if surveys show little activity within the connecting strip itself.

The researchers were careful about the limits of their method. Powder might stick differently from real pollen, and a sheltered route useful to one insect might not suit another. They recommended combining movement markers with observations of plant reproduction before drawing up a permanent habitat plan. The value of the trial was to reveal a connection that simple visitor counts had overlooked.

questions.prompt: Why are insect counts alone insufficient for the researchers’ purpose?
options: They can be carried out only at night.
They reveal every successful pollination event.
They do not show whether pollen moves between habitat patches.
They exclude insects that remain on a flower.
questions.answer: They do not show whether pollen moves between habitat patches.
questions.explanation: 访花数量反映当地活动，却不能证明昆虫在不同生境之间携带花粉。

questions.prompt: What was the purpose of the fluorescent powder?
options: To make the insects easier to breed.
To trace possible movement between flowers.
To protect flowers from strong winds.
To replace nutrients missing from the soil.
questions.answer: To trace possible movement between flowers.
questions.explanation: 荧光粉作为临时标记，用于追踪花朵间可能的传播路线。

questions.prompt: What role did the uncut grass strip appear to play?
options: It offered a sheltered route for some insects.
It prevented all insects from reaching the channel.
It increased the amount of natural pollen on every flower.
It provided the main nesting site for the entire population.
questions.answer: It offered a sheltered route for some insects.
questions.explanation: 视频显示，部分昆虫在风较大时沿未修剪草带移动，以获得遮挡。

questions.prompt: What additional evidence did the team recommend collecting?
options: Records of the price of agricultural land.
A count of lamps used during the investigation.
Measurements of how quickly the powder faded in storage.
Observations of whether plants reproduced successfully.
questions.answer: Observations of whether plants reproduced successfully.
questions.explanation: 荧光粉并不等同于实际授粉结果，需结合植物繁殖表现判断。
